steps.title: Acute interstitial nephritis
steps.body: Triad of fever, rash, and eosinophilia after a drug exposure (beta-lactams, TMP-SMX, NSAIDs, PPIs, rifampin, allopurinol, amoxicillin). AKI with sterile pyuria, WBC casts, and mild proteinuria; urinalysis can be bland early.
steps.tip: Stop the culprit drug and give corticosteroids when kidney function is not recovering — supported by KDIGO AKI guidance.

steps.title: Chronic tubulointerstitial disease
steps.body: Slow, bland, non-nephrotic proteinuria (<1 g/day), sterile pyuria, concentrating defect, and papillary necrosis. Analgesic nephropathy (phenacetin/NSAID), reflux nephropathy, and genetic tubulointerstitial kidney diseases (e.g., HNF1B, MUC1) show small kidneys with cortical scarring.
steps.tip: Analgesic nephropathy classically shows papillary necrosis with calcification on CT.

steps.title: Renal tubular acidosis patterns
steps.body: Distal (type 1): urine pH stays >5.3 with nephrolithiasis. Proximal (type 2): urine pH falls once serum bicarbonate is low. Type 4: hyperkalemic with low/normal ammonium excretion, seen in diabetic CKD and ACEi/ARB use.
steps.tip: Urine anion gap helps separate distal (positive) from proximal/GI bicarbonate loss (negative).

steps.title: ADPKD diagnosis and prognosis
steps.body: KDIGO 2025: ultrasound criteria by age in at-risk adults, and in adults with incidentally found cysts without family history, use contrast-enhanced MRI or CT plus genetic testing. Prognostication uses age, eGFR, kidney size, hypertension, and genotype ( Mayo Imaging Classification, PROPKD).
steps.tip: A negative ultrasound reliably excludes ADPKD in at-risk adults aged 30-39; in adults under 30 a negative study is not sufficient.

steps.title: ADPKD management
steps.body: Tight blood pressure control (<110/75 if tolerated), RAAS blockade first line, sodium restriction, tolvaptan for patients at risk of rapid progression, high water intake for vasopressin-exposed early disease, and avoid nephrotoxins, dehydration, and unnecessary imaging contrast.
steps.tip: Tolvaptan requires aquaresis precautions, liver monitoring, and is avoided in pregnancy and in those unable to sense thirst.
